title: JWST Observations of RR Lyrae in Leo P
comment: 17 pages, 16 figures, 2 tables, includes appendix, Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We analyze co-spatial HST/ACS and JWST/NIRCam time-series photometric observations of RR Lyrae in the low-metallicity dwarf galaxy Leo P. This study provides a new opportunity to explore the properties of and potential for metal-poor RR Lyrae studies with JWST using well-understood relationships from past HST work. We identify 20 RR Lyrae in the HST imaging and 15 RR Lyrae in the JWST imaging. We determine the periods, amplitudes, and mean magnitudes for each of the RR Lyrae. We fit the Period-Wesenheit-Metallicity (PWZ) function to the HST RR Lyrae population, and obtain a Gaia-consistent RR Lyrae-based distance to Leo P of $μ= 26.04\pm0.07$ ($1.61\pm0.06$ Mpc), consistent with existing distance measurements. We determine a JWST-based PWZ using Leo P data along with previous JWST RR Lyrae observations in WLM. The simultaneous fit decreases the mean fractional uncertainty by 31% on the slope and by 11% on the intercept, increasing the constraining power as compared to the existing calibration.

title: The Impact of High-Mass Clusters on the Binary Black Hole Merger Rate over Cosmic Time
comment: 16 pages, 11 figures. Submitted to ApJ. Comments welcome!
summary: We present a cosmological calculation of the binary black hole merger rate from dense star clusters, using a $\texttt{Cluster Monte Carlo}$ ($\texttt{CMC}$) model grid spanning the full observed parameter space of cluster mass, metallicity, and virial radius. For the first time, we incorporate $N=10^{7}$-particle $\texttt{CMC}$ models into this calculation, including a new solar-metallicity model, extending the $\texttt{CMC Cluster Catalog}$ to the most massive clusters observed in the local Universe. Using an analytic cluster formation model which convolves the cluster formation rate with delay-time distributions from our model suite, we find that the local cluster BBH merger rate is dominated by low-mass ($M_1 \lesssim 20\,M_\odot$) mergers originating from recently formed, high-metallicity clusters. While high-mass clusters are the primary sites of hierarchical (second-generation and higher) mergers, their contribution to the overall merger rate is suppressed by the exponential cutoff of the cluster initial mass function. The hierarchical merger rate is therefore highly sensitive to the exact value of the Schechter mass, $M_S$, suggesting that gravitational wave constraints on the hierarchical merger fraction can independently constrain the high-mass end of the cluster initial mass function. Our cluster formation model reproduces the observed present-day GC number density without fine tuning, and we find $M_S = 10^7\,M_\odot$ provides the best match to the observed Virgo GC mass distribution. For this value, $27\%$ of local dynamical mergers are hierarchical, compared to $18\%$ for the canonical value of $M_S = 10^{6.26}\,M_\odot$. Our merger weights, which we make publicly available, can be used for direct comparison with LVK distributions and other formation models.

title: CoRGI in MaNGA - II. NGC 5717: cold-gas accretion and disk growth in a BGG
comment: 17 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables, submitted to A&A
summary: Large-scale stellar counter-rotation, in which two coplanar stellar components rotate in opposite directions, is usually interpreted as a signature of external gas accretion. Such systems are most often found in relatively sparse environments, where cold gas can be acquired and remain dynamically undisturbed long enough to settle into a disk. It is less clear whether this channel can operate in massive central galaxies, whose group or cluster environments can heat, strip, or perturb cold gas. Here we present NGC 5717, one of the most massive galaxies known to host a counter-rotating stellar disk and the first identified case in a brightest group galaxy. Using integral-field spectroscopy from SDSS-IV Mapping Nearby Galaxies at Apache Point Observatory (MaNGA), together with CFHT imaging, ancillary HI data, and SDSS/DESI spectroscopy of the surrounding group, we show that the galaxy contains a dynamically cold counter-rotating disk embedded in an old dynamically hot elliptical component. The disk is young ($\sim 1.3$ Gyr), metal-poor ([Fe/H] $\sim -0.7$ dex), extended ($h \sim 2.4$ kpc), and massive ($\log M_\star/M_\odot \sim 9.9$); the associated ionized gas co-rotates with it, while the available HI data indicate no significant remaining reservoir of neutral atomic gas ($\log M_{\mathrm{HI}}/M_\odot \lesssim 9$). These properties support an in situ origin of the secondary component from externally accreted gas. The chemical evolution model favors gas accretion from a cosmic filament, which is consistent with the surrounding cosmic-web geometry, and indicates highly efficient burst-like star formation with substantial metal-enriched outflows. NGC 5717 may therefore represent a rare example of disk growth in a massive central galaxy, enabled by external cold-gas accretion during an earlier phase of the group assembly history.

title: How Little Red Dots Turn Blue: Evolution of Kelvin-Helmholtz Contracting Black Hole Envelopes and Observational Diagnostics
comment: 26 pages, 12 figures. Submitted to ApJ. Comments are welcome!
summary: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations have revealed compact, red-colored, broad-line emitters known as little red dots (LRDs), while a bluer counterpart population has been referred to as little blue dots (LBDs). Their physical connection remains unclear: they may represent different evolutionary stages of the same phenomenon, distinct populations, or different phases of the broader evolution of early galaxies and their black holes (BHs). We propose a model in which a rapidly growing BH is embedded in a geometrically thick gaseous envelope accompanied by concurrent nuclear star formation. The model reproduces the observed spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of LRDs and LBDs, and naturally connects the two phases through Kelvin-Helmholtz contraction of the envelope and exposure of the nuclear accretion disk, as the gas supply declines due to external stellar activity or feedback. We predict the corresponding evolutionary tracks in the UV-optical slope ($β_{\rm UV}$-$β_{\rm opt}$) plane which bridge the apparent gap between LRDs and LBDs. These evolutionary tracks start from the LRD regime and consistently exhibit a red excursion that extends toward $(β_{\rm UV},β_{\rm opt})\sim(2,-1)$ before turning toward the LBD regime. This feature is largely insensitive to variations in the model parameters that govern the envelope structure, providing a robust signature of the transitional population. The transition lasts $\sim5$-$50\,\mathrm{Myr}$, depending primarily on the BH feedback efficiency and the gas-retention efficiency of the envelope. The abundance ratio of transitional systems to LRDs therefore provides a constraint on BH feedback and gas retention during the rapid growth of early supermassive BHs.

title: A Parsec-scale Circumstellar Shell Around VX Sgr: Mass Loss and RSG/TŻO Nature
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: A thin, arc-shaped shell is discovered surrounding VX Sagittarii (VX Sgr), the largest known CSM shell around an RSG at a scale $r\sim0.59\,\mathrm{pc}$. The nebula has an extinction-corrected H$α$ intensity $I_{\mathrm{H}α}\sim38\,\mathrm{R}$ and an ionized mass $\sim0.1\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. The slow $12\,\mathrm{km\,s}^{-1}$ peculiar velocity of VX Sgr and the lack of far-infrared emission in the arc indicate that it is not produced by a bow shock, but is likely instead steady RSG wind or ejecta that is photoionized by a nearby $\mathrm{O}$- or $\mathrm{B}$- type star. The nature of VX Sgr is debated in the literature as a red supergiant/hypergiant (RSG/RHG), super-AGB star, or Thorne--Żytkow Object (TŻO). Using the kinematic age of the Sgr OB1 association, the super-AGB model is disfavored. A spectroscopic test of the arc is proposed to potentially distinguish an RSG from a possible TŻO. The mass-loss rate is estimated from the geometry and emission measure of the shell, finding $\dot{M}\approx4\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. The future interaction of the supernova (SN) ejecta of VX Sgr and the surrounding circumstellar material (CSM) is briefly explored through the mass ratio $Λ$ of the shell and SN ejecta; the interaction would likely not have a significant effect on the SN forward shock.

title: The Pristine survey XXIX. Data Release 2: Photometric metallicities for 15 millions stars down to $G\sim 20.5$
comment: accepted for publication in A&A. The Pristine DR2 is available at https://zenodo.org/records/21092750
summary: Tailored narrow-band photometric observations are an efficient way to measure the metallicity of Milky Way stars. The Pristine survey has been mapping the northern sky since 2015 using narrow-band $CaHK$ photometry obtained with the MegaCam imager on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope (CFHT). Data Release 1 (DR1) provided a high-precision absolute calibration of the survey observed before October 2022 using \Gaia DR3 XP synthetic photometry, yielding photometric metallicities over $\sim$6,500 deg$^2$, but was limited in depth to the availability of \Gaia spectro-photometry ($G \lesssim 17.65$). We present the Pristine Data Release 2 (DR2) that includes all Pristine observations until January 2025, corresponding to an additional 1,500\,deg$^2$ of coverage, and including all faint sources down to $G\sim20.5$. This release aims to exploit the full depth of the Pristine observations to uncover the faint metal-poor halo. We process all images observed from the start of the survey in March 2015 through to January 2025 following the methodology presented in DR1. The core of the calibration utilizes the subset of bright stars with \Gaia synthetic $CaHK_\mathrm{syn}$ magnitudes to train the \texttt{PhotCalib} neural network. We then derive photometric metallicities using the established Pristine ($CaHK, G, G_{\rm BP}, G_{\rm RP}$) to [Fe/H] model. The resulting catalogue covers approximately $\sim$ 8,000 deg$^{2}$ and provides photometric metallicities for 15 millions FGK stars, which show good agreement with recently published, independent Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) metallicities. With its increased coverage and access to a significantly fainter regime compared to DR1, DR2 significantly increases the volume of the survey. We report more than 200,000 and 6,500 very and extremely metal-poor star candidates, respectively.

title: A Search for Dust in the Outflow of the HH212 Class 0 Protostellar System
comment: 25 pages, 9 figures. Accepted for publication in AJ
summary: Perhaps the most visually striking phenomenon during star formation is the ejection of material along the direction of the protostar's rotational axis. Observed in the form of molecular outflows and/or atomic jets, these features carry away mass, energy and angular momentum from the system. Given the known dust content of protoplanetary disks, and the energetics of outflows, it has been suggested that it should be possible to lift dust from disks via winds, yet limited observational evidence has been presented in the literature. Any detection of dust within protostellar outflows not only puts constraints on the dust content in outflows, but if a sufficient amount of dust can be removed from the system, the mass budget for planet formation could also be affected. We present re-imaging of archival, multi-frequency dust continuum observations taken with the Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) towards the HH212 protostellar system. We detect an extension in the dust emission, and using multi-frequency data in Bands 7 and 9, we estimate the spectral index of the emitting dust and the dust mass in the wind launching region. We find a small but still significant amount of dust mass coincident with the molecular outflow cavity. This finding is assessed in relation to the hypothesis that the outflow could be capable of transporting dust away from the HH212 protoplanetary disk.

title: HI rotation curves and mass-size relation for 568 galaxies from the Apertif Wide-area Extragalactic Survey
comment: Published in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: The extended HI rotation curves of galaxies are one of the most powerful tools for studying galaxy evolution and for testing different dark matter and modified gravity models. However, their sample sizes have historically been limited to a few hundred galaxies, mostly due to the survey speed of radio interferometers. Here, we present a first data release of HI kinematic models from the Apertif Wide-area Extragalactic Survey (AWES). Starting from 1924 galaxies detected in HI, we constructed 568 reliable kinematic models, which provide rotation curves, velocity dispersion profiles, surface density profiles, and HI disk geometries. This dataset constitutes the largest homogeneous HI rotation curve sample to date. The HI disks of the modeled galaxies span three orders of magnitude in HI mass, have outer rotation velocities between ~20 and ~300 km/s, and extend from 2 to more than 60 kpc. The number of data points of the rotation curves ranges from 3 to 23, with a peak value at 4 and a broad tail to larger values. The rotation curves display a variety of inner shapes, but in general, they tend to become flat at large radii. Based on the HI surface density profiles derived during the kinematic modeling, we studied the HI mass-size relation with a large homogeneous sample of 213 galaxies. The relation is very tight, with an observed scatter along the mass direction of ~0.101 dex and an inferred intrinsic scatter along the same direction of only 0.067 +/- 0.007 dex. The best fitting slope is 1.96 +/- 0.03 when fitting for mass as a function of size, indicating that HI disks have a constant average surface density.

title: Beyond Mergers: the Role of Metallicity in Forming a Reservoir of Massive and Detached Binary Black Hole Systems
comment: 17 pages, 8 figures
summary: Isolated binary evolution is a key pathway to forming binary black hole (BBH) mergers. However, the observed gravitational-wave population indicates it may not account for all mergers, especially those with high primary black hole mass ($\gtrsim 30 M_{\odot}$). Using the binary population synthesis code \texttt{POSYDON}, we simulate populations of binary systems at eight metallicities from $10^{-4}$ to $2\,Z_\odot$ and classify each BH-forming binary as a merging BBH, a detached BBH, or a system disrupted during BH formation. We find that metallicity shapes these populations differently, especially for high BH masses ($\gtrsim 25 M_{\odot}$). At lower metallicities, between $10^{-2}$ and $0.45\,Z_\odot$, massive BHs continue to form but become increasingly unlikely to merge: the number of massive merging BBHs declines sharply, while the detached population remains abundant. For $25$--$35\,M_\odot$ BHs, the detached-to-merging ratio increases by more than two orders of magnitude across this metallicity range. After weighting by cosmic star formation, massive BHs are found predominantly in detached binaries with orbital periods $\gtrsim 10^2$ days. Therefore, isolated binary evolution can form massive BBHs even if it rarely produces massive BBH mergers, leaving behind a massive and detached population that may be driven to merger through dynamical interactions in dense stellar environments.

title: Wandering intermediate-mass black holes and off-nuclear tidal disruption events from early star clusters
comment: 27 pages, 11 figures
summary: Off-nuclear tidal disruption events (TDEs) reveal evidence for massive black holes outside galactic centers, but the origins of this wandering population remain uncertain. We investigate wandering intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs) formed through runaway stellar collisions in dense, high-redshift star clusters and predict their TDE signatures across cosmic time. Our semi-analytic model samples clusters associated with low-mass subhalos at $7<z<20$ and uses merger trees from the IllustrisTNG TNG50 simulation to follow the assembly of 15 elliptical galaxies with stellar masses of $10^9-10^{11}~M_\odot$. We compare two models for high-redshift cluster formation: a maximal model taken from a high-resolution simulation and a conservative model calibrated from local cluster relations. Off-nuclear TDEs produced through this mechanism occur in bursts within 10-100 Myr of IMBH formation as the loss-cone surrounding the black hole is depleted. We estimate the rate of off-nuclear TDEs expected across time per galaxy, and characterize these events as typically occurring between $10-10^3$ kpc from their host galaxy centers. Event rates increase with galaxy mass; in the maximal model, the progenitors of the most massive galaxies reach peak off-nuclear TDE rates of approximately $5\times10^{-4}-4\times10^{-2}~\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ per galaxy at $7\lesssim z\lesssim13$. This work provides a framework for constraining the early population of star clusters that form IMBHs through runaway collapse via their contribution to the rate of off-nuclear TDEs in the high redshift Universe.

authors: M. J. P. F. G. Monteiro
title: EPRV Asteroseismology of the K dwarfs GJ 570 A and GJ 783 A with ESPRESSO. Empirical mode-amplitude scaling in tension with 3D convection simulations
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Solar-like oscillations in K dwarfs have intrinsically low amplitudes, making them challenging to detect in space-based photometry. The advent of Extremely Precise Radial Velocity (EPRV) instrumentation enables Doppler asteroseismology in the mid-K regime, providing a new opportunity to test mode-excitation and damping physics. We investigate the scaling of oscillation amplitudes with stellar parameters and assess whether 3D surface convection simulations reproduce the observed amplitude behavior. High-cadence ESPRESSO radial-velocity time series were obtained over five and six consecutive nights for the K dwarfs GJ 570 A (K4 V) and GJ 783 A (K2.5 V), respectively. We identified oscillation modes from weighted power spectra and extracted them via sine-wave fitting following spectral deconvolution. Peak mode amplitudes were measured from heavily smoothed power spectra. For comparison, we performed 3D radiative-hydrodynamical simulations including excitation and damping-rate calculations. We measured 6 modes for GJ 570 A and 24 for GJ 783 A ($\ell=0$-$2$, and $\ell=3$ for GJ 783 A). The peak radial-mode amplitudes are $2.57 \pm 0.52\:{\rm cm\,s^{-1}}$ and $4.90 \pm 0.81\:{\rm cm\,s^{-1}}$, respectively. These results support a transition from an $\sim(L/M)^{0.7}$ amplitude scaling to a steeper $\sim(L/M)^{1.5}$ scaling, occurring near the G/K-dwarf boundary toward decreasing $L/M$. In contrast, 3D simulations predict an $\sim(L/M)^{0.9}$ scaling for K dwarfs, revealing tension between observations and first-principles convection models. EPRV asteroseismology extends into the mid-K regime and exposes a steep mode-amplitude scaling that our 3D convection simulations do not reproduce. This discrepancy points to missing physics in our implementation of convection-pulsation coupling and/or limitations in the adopted modeling assumptions, motivating further theoretical investigation.

title: An Attenuation Bump at z=9.3: Probing Dust Diversity at Cosmic Dawn
comment: paper submitted to ApJ, Figure 8 summarizes the key finding of this work
summary: We report the identification of a UV attenuation bump in the Black Pearl, a galaxy at a spectroscopic redshift of 9.3335 observed with JWST/NIRSpec as part of the ZENITH and EMBER surveys. This is the highest-redshift UV bump reported to date, probing dust properties only approximately 500 Myr after the Big Bang. The feature is directly detected as a broad depression in the rest-frame UV continuum and is well described by a local Drude profile, with a central wavelength of 2132+/-17 Angstroms, an FWHM of 413+/-54 Angstroms, and a peak attenuation of 0.21+/-0.02 mag. Joint spectrophotometric modeling with a flexible attenuation law independently recovers a pronounced UV bump without imposing its presence a priori, regardless of the adopted star-formation history. The modeling indicates a relatively low-mass, actively star-forming galaxy, with a logarithmic stellar mass of 8.35 (+0.09/-0.08) in solar units, a star-formation rate of 2.36 (+0.54/-0.42) solar masses per year, and a visual attenuation of 0.34 (+0.12/-0.11) mag. Rest-frame optical emission-line diagnostics indicate a hard ionizing spectrum and allow for a moderate AGN contribution, but provide no evidence for a powerful AGN capable of dominating the observed UV continuum. The bump is blueshifted by 43+/-17 Angstroms (approximately 2.5 sigma) relative to the canonical Milky Way 2175 Angstrom feature and by 127 +/- 17 Angstroms relative to the few UV bumps currently known at redshift approximately 7, while its width is consistent with the broad distribution measured along Milky Way sightlines. The displaced central wavelength therefore provides the clearest evidence for a nonstandard UV-bump profile at redshift 9.3335, pointing to substantial diversity in the properties of UV-bump carriers at early cosmic times, with both PAHs and small graphite grains remaining plausible candidates.

title: Finite-Element Asteroseismology I: Two-Dimensional Adiabatic Oscillations of Rapidly Rotating N=3 Polytropes
comment: Submitted to MNRAS. Comments welcome
summary:
We develop a finite-element formulation for linear adiabatic oscillations of axisymmetric uniformly rotating, centrifugally distorted, self-gravitating N=3 polytropes. Equilibrium models are constructed using self-consistent-field iteration and then remeshed on a surface-fitted oblate meridional domain. The quadratic eigenvalue problem describing oscillations for each azimuthal wavenumber $m$ is solved using a conforming two-domain mesh. The density-weighted displacement, $\boldsymbol{u}=ρ^{1/2}\boldsymbolξ$, is defined in the stellar interior, whereas the gravitational-potential perturbation $δΦ$ is solved both inside the star and in an exterior vacuum. The coupled displacement--potential problem is assembled and solved within FEniCSx as a polynomial eigenvalue problem.
  Without rotation, the axisymmetric modes agree closely with an independent one-dimensional calculation. For finite rotation rates, several clean axisymmetric $p$-mode branches of the spheroidal star successfully reproduce the frequencies tabulated by Reese (2006). The relative frequency differences induced by rotation are smaller than $3\times10^{-4}$ for the low-order mode branches up to $\sim 60$\% of the critical rotation rate. These tests validate both the centrifugally distorted equilibrium and the finite-element implementation.
  We develop a method to track eigenfunctions continuously as a function of rotation and decompose their angular structure to quantify rotational mode mixing and progressive coupling between different spherical harmonic components. This reveals continuous deformation of individual mode branches from nearly single-$\ell$ structures to strongly mixed states at rapid rotation.
  This work is intended as a step toward finite-element multidimensional asteroseismology frameworks for modelling realistic rotationally and tidally distorted stellar configurations.

title: A model for the ongoing subcluster interaction in Centaurus
comment: Submitted to Astronomy and Astrophysics; comments welcome
summary: Intracluster globular clusters (GCs) preserve the hierarchical and chemical history of galaxy cluster assembly. The nearby Centaurus cluster is believed to be undergoing an interaction between two subclusters, Cen 30 and Cen 45, which should leave an imprint on its intracluster GCs. We aim to characterise the GC population in Centaurus and constrain its recent assembly history, ultimately constructing an interaction scenario consistent with the observational evidence. Using deep VLT/FORS imaging in the $V$ and $I$ bands, we select GC candidates around the cluster centre based on morphology and colour criteria. We use a Voronoi tessellation approach to study the GC spatial distribution and density profiles, demonstrating its advantages over traditional annuli-based methods. We then constrain the evolution of the galaxy luminosity function using the GC specific frequency and colour distribution. The GC spatial distribution shows significant substructure. As in other clusters, red GCs are concentrated on the brightest galaxies, whereas blue GCs trace a more extended structure. We confirm and quantify the previously reported 'bridge' of GCs connecting NGC 4696 and NGC 4709, showing that it hosts twice as many GCs as expected from the projected GC systems of the two galaxies alone. The inferred evolution of the galaxy luminosity function agrees with previous results for Hydra I, yielding a faint-end slope of $α=-1.87_{-0.06}^{+0.06}$ for the galaxy population that assembled the Centaurus core. We propose a nearly head-on collision scenario in which Cen 45 recently passed through Cen 30, with the two subclusters moving approximately along the line of sight. This scenario explains the large line-of-sight velocity difference between the subclusters, the hot X-ray-emitting gas between them, the GC bridge, and the puffed-up GC system of NGC 4709.

title: An HST survey of photometry and multiplicity of brown dwarfs and planetary-mass objects in the field of Taurus
comment: 19 pages, 10 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We present a photometric and multiplicity survey of 26 young objects with masses between 6 Mj and 37 Mj and spectral type later than M8 in the Taurus star-forming region with the Hubble Space Telescope. We search for companion candidates using two methods: a dedicated photometric technique based on the combination of colours from multi-band photometry and point spread function fitting. No companion candidates are detected beyond 30 au. With an updated membership and age identification, we determine luminosity, temperature, and mass for the 26 young objects using evolutionary models. We demonstrate that our HST observations are sensitive to companions down to masses of 1 Mj and even lower for some targets by artificial star injection tests. After survey completeness correction, we derive a binary frequency < 6.5% for this sample in the 68% confidence interval for companions with mass ratios between 0.1 and 1 and separations between 30 and 7,000 au. We find no significant difference in binary frequency among planetary-mass objects in Taurus, Upper Scorpius, and the field. These findings support that the binary frequency of planetary-mass objects is settled at young ages, probably younger than 1--10 Myr, suggesting that the formation of wide-orbit planetary-mass binaries is inefficient and the disruption of them likely occurs at a very early stage in a low density environment.

title: The ALMA-QUARKS Survey. IV. Core Mass Function and Evolutionary Trends in Core Formation Efficiency and Chemistry
comment: 28 pages, 14 figures, submitted to the ApJS
summary: The ALMA-QUARKS (Querying Underlying Mechanisms of Massive Star Formation with ALMA-Resolved Gas Kinematics and Structures) survey targets 139 massive protoclusters selected from the ATOMS survey. The targets were observed at 1.3~mm wavelength with an angular resolution of $\sim0.3^{\prime\prime}$, corresponding to $\sim10^3$~au at the sample's median distance of $\sim3.8$~kpc. Using \texttt{getsf}, we identify 3374 dense cores and classify them as starless, protostellar, hot core, or H{\sc ii} region candidates based on spectral-line diagnostics (e.g., H30$α$, CH$_3$CN, and CH$_3$OH) and CO outflow associations. The resulting catalog provides core physical properties and enables statistical investigations of dense core populations in massive protocluster environments. The derived global core mass function (CMF) after excluding H{\sc ii} region candidates, which is biased by distance effects, has a relatively flat power-law slope at the high-mass end ($\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}\log M \propto M^{-γ}$, with $γ=0.98\pm0.03$). In contrast, the measured high-mass slopes in individual distance bins are approximately Salpeter-like, while their fitted lower mass limits increase with distance. We further examine the core formation efficiency (CFE) across the full sample and find that it positively correlates with the luminosity-to-mass ratio of the parental clumps, consistent with an evolutionary increase in the fraction of mass concentrated into dense cores. We also investigate the detection rates of different molecular tracers and find systematic chemical variations with evolutionary stage. Compared with the ASHES survey, we find that the detection rates of deuterated species vary significantly even for cores at the same evolutionary stages, suggesting an important environmental influence on the chemical evolution of cores.

title: Intermediate- and high-resolution optical spectroscopy on the nascent planetary nebula Vy 2-2: Evidence of binary-star evolution
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. 14 pages, 5 figures, 8 tables
summary: Planetary nebulae (PNe) tend to show spectacular non-spherical shapes whose origin is not fully understood. Crucial information about PNe formation can be obtained by studying their very first stages. We present and analyze new intermediate- and échelle high-resolution spectra of the nascent PN Vy 2-2 to obtain its chemical abundances and a new value for its controversial Abundance Discrepancy Factor (ADF), investigate the internal kinematics and ionization of the nebula, and infer its possible formation processes. Our intermediate resolution spectra reveal many previously unreported nebular recombination (e.g., N$^+$) and forbidden (e.g., [F IV]) emission lines as well as stellar emission lines. Some of the newly detected nebular lines are important to determine the ADF. The derived abundances are subsolar and agree with previous values, while the new value of the ADF(O$^{2+}$)=13.6$\pm$2.6 indicates that Vy 2-2 belongs to the group of PNe with unusually high ADF. Our morphokinematical and ionization structure analysis reveals that Vy 2-2 consists of a relatively high-excitation central region and two low-excitation bipolar lobes. Our data does not show significant shock excitation in the main ionized shell of this PN. A distance of ~1.68 kpc to Vy 2-2 is obtained from the published angular expansion of the central region and its expansion velocity in H$^+$. The inferred kinematical age of ~210 yr supports that Vy 2-2 is a nascent PN. The stellar emission lines suggest a wels-like spectrum although more likely associated with an irradiated close companion than with the central star. Actually, the unusually high ADF, the observed nebular structures, presence of F, among others, point to Vy 2-2 hosting a post-common-envelope binary system. Chemical abundances and circumstellar mass estimates suggest an initial mass $\lesssim$0.9 $M_{\odot}$ for the star progenitor of Vy 2-2.

title: The optical colors of hidden spiral-like features in nine Virgo early--type dwarfs
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: Dwarf early-type galaxies (ETGs) are abundant in nearby clusters and provide a key laboratory for studying environmentally driven galaxy transformation. Although dwarf ETGs were once considered structurally simple, deep imaging has revealed embedded spiral-like features (e.g., bars and spiral arms) in some of them, contributing only a small fraction of the total light. Their origin at dwarf scales remains uncertain. As a pilot study, we investigate spiral-like features in nine Virgo dwarf ETGs with clear embedded arms, using optical colors to test whether these features differ from the surrounding diffuse component, which would constrain their formation pathways. Using deep g- and i-band NGVS images, we apply a residual-based method to separate excess light associated with the spiral-like component from the diffuse host. The residual images define arm and interarm regions, enabling direct measurements of light fractions and g-i colors for both components. The spiral-like features contribute only a few percent of the total light (about 1.5-5.5% in i and 1.7-3.7% in g). We find a diverse range of colors across the sample: four galaxies host spiral-like features redder than their interarm regions, four show no robust arm-interarm color difference, and one exhibits a distinctly bluer spiral-like component. The latter is consistent with a recently quenched transition object, while the redder and color-uniform features are consistent with older or more metal-rich stellar populations. Spiral-like features in Virgo dwarf ETGs thus exhibit a surprising diversity in their photometric properties, implying multiple evolutionary channels rather than a single one. This pilot analysis also demonstrates readiness for the much larger NGVS sample of dwarfs with potential spiral-like features.

title: Influence of numerical domain design in simulations of solar coronal heating with the MAGEC code
summary: Numerical simulations are essential for studying the solar atmosphere, especially in the context of the coronal heating problem. Understanding how numerical factors and boundary conditions (BC) influence the energetic structure of these models is crucial for unraveling coronal heating mechanisms. We investigate how the computational domain dimensions, upper BC, and vertical grid resolution influence the relaxed thermal structure, energetics, and long-term stability of 2D solar atmosphere simulations with a vertical magnetic field. Using the MAGEC code, we conducted parametric studies varying domain width and height, vertical grid stretching, and top BC, including hot-plate, closed, unrestricted temperature, background heating, and non-reflecting characteristic configurations. We evaluated average temperature profiles for parameter dependence and temporal stability, and analyzed the energetic budget as a function of height, isolating contributions from radiative losses, thermal conduction, pressure work, and internal energy flux. Models with larger vertical domains show higher average coronal temperatures and steeper transition region gradients. Among the less artificial BC, non-reflecting characteristics most effectively delay coronal cooling. We determined the threshold height at which a dynamic top BC can mimic fixed-temperature setups, and established the maximum allowable grid stretching that preserves physical accuracy while reducing computational costs. The energetic terms change significantly with the chosen BC, with specific mechanisms acting as cooling agents in different atmospheric layers. Our results demonstrate that domain height, vertical grid design, and BC critically dictate the relaxed thermal structure and energetic balance of the simulated solar atmosphere.

title: Self Calibrated Galaxy Groups from the DESI DR1 Bright Galaxy Survey
comment: 32 pages, 26 Figures, submitted to ApJ. See https://ianw89.github.io/catalogs.html or https://data.desi.lbl.gov/doc/releases/dr1/#value-added-catalogs to acquire the catalog
summary: We present a galaxy group catalog built from Data Release 1 of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Bright Galaxy Survey, using the Self Calibrated Group Finder. The algorithm uses clustering data from the observed sample to calibrate the Group Finder's free parameters, rather than simulations. The catalog contains 2,229,741 galaxies from ~$2680$ deg$^2$ of sky with 3-pass coverage and $r$-band fluxes $\lt 19.5$. The catalog classifies all galaxies in the flux-limited sample as centrals or satellites and estimates host dark matter halo masses. We show the satellite fraction $f_{\rm sat}$, luminosity halo mass relation, stellar halo mass relation and halo occupation distributions (HODs) from the catalog. We find these non-parametric HODs can be fit by standard HOD models, with satellite power-law index $α$ values around 0.75 for star-forming galaxies and around 1.1 for quiescent objects. In agreement with recent results, we find that the quenched fraction of central galaxies depends mostly on halo mass and is nearly independent of central galaxy stellar mass for galaxies more massive than $10^{10.3}$ $M_\odot h^{-1}$ and halos more massive than $10^{12.2}$ $M_\odot h^{-1}$. In an appendix, we introduce a new Hybrid Nearest Neighbor (HNN) technique to mitigate systematics from fiber incompleteness. HNN uses photometric redshifts and multiple on-sky neighbors to assign redshifts to unobserved targets. Calibrated on DESI Survey Validation 3 data, our technique yields correct redshifts $\sim 50\%$ of the time and produces unbiased halo occupation statistics.

title: Investigation of an X-class Flare and Quasi-Periodic Pulsations in NOAA AR 13842 using SDO, Aditya-L1 and Solar Orbiter
comment: 23 Pages, 14 Figures, Accepted in Advances in Space Research (ASR)
summary: We investigate an X9.0 class flare (SOL2024-10-03T12:08) and associated quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs) in NOAA active region (AR) 13842 using observations from the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), Aditya-L1 and Solar Orbiter (SO). To explore the role of magnetic configuration in the flare, we employ non-force-free-field extrapolation technique for reconstructing a sequence of the coronal magnetic field throughout the flare. The observations reveal the emergence of intricate flare brightenings and ribbons. QPPs are observed with periods of $\approx$ 2 and $\approx$ 6 minutes in EUV, $\approx$ 7 minutes in UV, and $\approx$ 1 minute in X-rays. The extrapolation documents the presence of a flux rope, a sheared arcade, and a hyperbolic flux tube (HFT) enveloping the rope and the arcade. The sequence of the extrapolation illustrates an increase in the twist of the rope as it ascends towards a torus-unstable region, thereby rendering the rope a viable candidate for eruption. The sheared arcade appears to generate electric current through its foot-point's motion, which explains the sigmoidal brightening observed at the flare onset. The motion also seems to drive the non-parallel field lines closer together, heightening gradient in the magnetic field beneath the rope. Consequently, recurrent magnetic reconnection is anticipated within the sheared arcade --- explaining the ascent of the rope with its twist increment. The formation of parallel flare ribbons is attributed to these reconnections. Furthermore, reconnection at the HFT is proposed to lead the remote and quasi-circular ribbons. Crucially, repeated reconnections inside the arcade as well as at the HFT are speculated to cause the QPPs.

title: JWST reveals a highly ionized nebula powered by an ultraluminous X-ray source with a massive black hole in the metal-poor galaxy Holmberg II
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures
summary: Recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations have revealed fine-structure lines of ions with ionization potentials ${\gtrsim}50$\,eV, such as [Ne\,{\sc v}] and [O\,{\sc iv}], in nebular spectra of some low-metallicity galaxies, raising questions about the nature of the ionizing sources. Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) have been considered as potential contributors, but direct evidence linking individual ULXs to highly ionized nebulae is limited. Here we present JWST IFU spectroscopy of the nebula surrounding the template ULX Ho\,II\,X--1 in the low-metallicity galaxy Holmberg\,II, already known to emit He\,{\sc ii}\,$\lambda4686$ and [O\,{\sc iv}]\,25.89\,$μ$m lines. We resolve the infrared nebula on spatial scales of ${\sim}15-25$\,pc and report the first detections of [Ne\,{\sc v}] and [Ne\,{\sc vi}] in this source. We find anisotropic ionizing conditions: emission from the highest-ionization species arises from compact regions offset from the ULX toward the previously detected radio knots, whereas lower-ionization species trace the wider nebula. The preferential alignment of the highest-ionization emission with the radio axis suggests anisotropic escape of the ionizing continuum and a physical connection with jet-ejection activity. Spectral lines across the nebula are narrow and consistent with the instrumental resolution, indicating kinematically quiescent gas and disfavoring shocks as the dominant ionization mechanism. Together, these results provide direct evidence linking an individual ULX to a highly ionized nebula in a low-metallicity galaxy. These JWST observations of Ho~II~X--1 show that an accreting black hole in a low-metallicity galaxy is responsible for the extreme ionization of the surrounding nebula on ${\sim}100$\,pc scales.

title: JWST Observations of RR Lyrae in Leo P
comment: 17 pages, 16 figures, 2 tables, includes appendix, Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We analyze co-spatial HST/ACS and JWST/NIRCam time-series photometric observations of RR Lyrae in the low-metallicity dwarf galaxy Leo P. This study provides a new opportunity to explore the properties of and potential for metal-poor RR Lyrae studies with JWST using well-understood relationships from past HST work. We identify 20 RR Lyrae in the HST imaging and 15 RR Lyrae in the JWST imaging. We determine the periods, amplitudes, and mean magnitudes for each of the RR Lyrae. We fit the Period-Wesenheit-Metallicity (PWZ) function to the HST RR Lyrae population, and obtain a Gaia-consistent RR Lyrae-based distance to Leo P of $μ= 26.04\pm0.07$ ($1.61\pm0.06$ Mpc), consistent with existing distance measurements. We determine a JWST-based PWZ using Leo P data along with previous JWST RR Lyrae observations in WLM. The simultaneous fit decreases the mean fractional uncertainty by 31% on the slope and by 11% on the intercept, increasing the constraining power as compared to the existing calibration.

title: ACACIAS II: element abundances for 39 stars in the dwarf galaxy Sculptor
summary: Element abundances in nearby galaxies provide insights into their chemical enrichment histories and place the Milky Way and its neighbours in a broader cosmological context. These systems can be studied through individual stars, whose resolved spectra enable the construction of a chemical abundance census of the Local Group. We present the second stage of the ACACIAS (extra-galactic ArChAeology with Cannon Inferred Abundances from resolved integral field unit Spectra) program, which aims to build the first homogeneous data set of stellar abundances across dwarf galaxies spanning a range of masses for comparison with Milky Way properties. We analyse low-resolution (R=1800), low-SNR (signal-to-noise ratio, ~ 25) MUSE spectra for 39 stars in the Sculptor dwarf spheroidal galaxy. Using the data-driven method The Cannon, we combine high-fidelity labels from the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) survey with MUSE-like Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) spectra to analyse the MUSE data. This enables the determination of [Mg/Fe], [Mn/Fe], [C/Fe], [N/Fe], and [Al/Fe] on the APOGEE abundance scale, with precisions of σ = 0.09-0.37 dex. Comparing model configurations, we show that [Mg/Fe], [Mn/Fe], and [C/Fe] are best recovered from targeted spectral windows, whereas stellar parameters and [Al/Fe] benefit from full-spectrum information with telluric masking. This reflects the complementary strengths of restricted-window models, which recover abundances from direct spectral features, and full-spectrum models, which exploit correlations with other labels when diagnostic features are weak or absent. Our approach demonstrates the potential of low-resolution, low-SNR stellar spectra to build homogeneous datasets for extragalactic archaeology to better understand the chemical enrichment diversity of the Local Group.

title: A machine-learning-driven dataset of 144,111 polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon infrared spectra for interpreting aromatic infrared bands
summary: The interpretation of interstellar aromatic infrared bands (AIBs) relies on reference spectral libraries, but the chemical space covered by existing databases remains incomplete relative to the vast structural diversity of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) expected in the interstellar medium. We present a large-scale, high-throughput PAH infrared (IR) spectral database that complements existing reference libraries by providing significantly more continuous coverage of the PAH chemical space for small to medium-sized PAHs. We used a machine-learning double-harmonic (ML-DH) framework that integrates neural network force fields with electronic dipole models. This framework achieves quantum-chemical accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost. It has been validated against independent density functional theory calculations and benchmark spectral databases. The resulting dataset comprises 144,111 IR spectra for 48,037 closed-shell, even-carbon benzenoid PAH structures across neutral, cationic, and anionic charge states, complete with per-spectrum uncertainty estimates. The spectral library, optimized geometries, and model code are publicly available. They can be used to complement existing libraries for interpreting and modeling JWST AIB observations and those from future IR missions.

title: ALMA observations towards M83 reveal N2H+ tracing dense gas
comment: Accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal, 27 pages, 12 figures
summary: Galactic observations have shown that N2H+ intensities preferentially trace star-forming dense molecular gas compared with HCN or HCO+, which are conventionally used as dense-gas tracers in extragalactic studies. In this study, we aim to verify this trend in the nearby star-forming galaxy M83. Using ALMA, we observed the J=1-0 transitions of N2H+ and HCN, along with the 1-mm and 3-mm continuum, and analyzed the archival CO(1-0) data. The data achieved a spatial resolution of 48 pc in the southwestern bar-end region of M83, covering an area of 2.1 kpc x 1.8 kpc. N2H+ and HCN intensities are approximately linearly correlated, indicating that HCN luminosity can still reasonably predict the amount of dense gas as well as N2H+ luminosity does. However, in regions with high column densities, N2H+ becomes a super-linear function of HCN, suggesting that the N2H+ emission is more sensitive to dense gas than HCN. We employed a radiative transfer model that predicts line intensities as a function of column density, adopting parametric column density probability distribution functions (N-PDFs) to describe the underlying column density distribution. The model demonstrates that the observed linear or superlinear trend can be explained by a log-normal distribution only or a log-normal and a power-law tail distribution in the N-PDF. Furthermore, the N2H+ intensity is significantly more sensitive to the power-law tail than the HCN intensity. In addition, our analysis incorporating archival data shows that N2H+ is a less reliable tracer of dense gas in galactic center regions, where warmer temperatures may promote N2H+ destruction.

title: An Energetic Consistency Test for Feedback-Driven Gas Loss in Milky Way Dwarf Satellites
comment: 15 pages, 2 figures
summary: Dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs) contain little detectable cold gas, but the relative roles of stellar feedback, reionization, and environmental effects in their gas loss remain uncertain. We apply an order-of-magnitude energy-budget test to nine Milky Way dwarf satellites using published color--magnitude-diagram star formation histories (SFHs), galaxy-level velocity dispersions, effective radii, and integrated $V$-band luminosities. For each galaxy and halo prescription, we define the energy-equivalence time $τ_{\mathrm{E}}$, when a crossing exists, as the first elapsed time at which the cumulative effective energy from core-collapse supernovae equals the adopted gas binding energy. This quantity is an energetic diagnostic rather than a direct measurement of wind launch. Under the fiducial parameters, all nine galaxies reach the nominal threshold under the kinematic--size prescription K+B16, yet star formation often continues long after threshold crossing. We compare the corresponding lookback time $t_{\mathrm{E,lb}}$ with $t_{90,\mathrm{lb}}$, the lookback time at which 90\% of the total initial stellar mass had formed. Because both times are derived from the same cumulative SFH, their temporal proximity is interpreted descriptively rather than as independent evidence of feedback-driven quenching. Whether the threshold is reached depends on the adopted halo mass, radius, retained gas fraction, and supernova--gas coupling efficiency. These results distinguish the availability of sufficient cumulative feedback energy from the processes that determine the timing of quenching.

title: A machine-learning-driven dataset of 144,111 polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon infrared spectra for interpreting aromatic infrared bands
summary: The interpretation of interstellar aromatic infrared bands (AIBs) relies on reference spectral libraries, but the chemical space covered by existing databases remains incomplete relative to the vast structural diversity of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) expected in the interstellar medium. We present a large-scale, high-throughput PAH infrared (IR) spectral database that complements existing reference libraries by providing significantly more continuous coverage of the PAH chemical space for small to medium-sized PAHs. We used a machine-learning double-harmonic (ML-DH) framework that integrates neural network force fields with electronic dipole models. This framework achieves quantum-chemical accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost. It has been validated against independent density functional theory calculations and benchmark spectral databases. The resulting dataset comprises 144,111 IR spectra for 48,037 closed-shell, even-carbon benzenoid PAH structures across neutral, cationic, and anionic charge states, complete with per-spectrum uncertainty estimates. The spectral library, optimized geometries, and model code are publicly available. They can be used to complement existing libraries for interpreting and modeling JWST AIB observations and those from future IR missions.

title: Disk tilts in Milky Way-like galaxies and their link to mergers
comment: 10 pages, 12 figures, submitted to A&A
summary: We investigated disk reorientation and its relationship to mergers in a sample of 93 Milky Way-mass galaxies drawn from the TNG50 simulations. From this sample, we identified 117 individual disk-tilt events with clearly defined start and end times, and we divided them into two classes based on whether the disk evolves smoothly or undergoes rapid disruption and regrowth during the tilt duration. For each tilt event, we linked the most massive merger that occurs in close temporal association with it. We focus on those tilt events occurring during phases of smooth disk evolution, which typically show tilt rates below 10 degrees per Gyr, persist for 2-9 Gyr, and are generally connected to minor mergers. Roughly 40% of these events reach tilt angles exceeding 30 degrees, most often triggered by satellites whose masses are comparable to or less massive than the galaxy's total stellar mass, merging on tangential orbits with orbital angular momentum that is retrograde or nearly perpendicular to the disk spin. The satellite consistently drives the disk tilt toward alignment with the satellite's orbital spin; satellites that came in on retrograde orbits relative to the disk spin can thus induce large tilt angles and can produce an almost orthogonal configuration between the stellar disk and the satellite's orbital plane as an intermediate phase. Owing to the comparatively slow tilt rates, the stellar disk can keep stable and continue to grow throughout the reorientation process. Consequently, galaxies that experience strong disk tilts can still maintain stellar disks that are as thin as those in systems without significant reorientation.

title: Are High-EW LAEs good analogs for the earliest galaxies? A study on the ionizing conditions and gas properties of LAEs at $2\lesssim z\lesssim7
comment: 18 pages, 8 figures, submitted to MNRAS
summary: Lyman-$α$ emitters (LAEs) are frequently proposed as analogs of the low-mass, metal-poor galaxies thought to dominate cosmic reionization. In particular, galaxies with large Ly$α$ equivalent widths (EWs) are expected to have not experienced significant chemical enrichment. We test this hypothesis using a sample of 88 LAEs at $2 \lesssim z\lesssim 7$, selected from MUSE observations that are undetected in deep HST imaging and subsequently followed up with JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy. Despite the unprecedented sensitivity of JWST, only 50 of the LAEs exhibit secure counterparts in available deep NIRCam imaging reaching typical 3$σ$ depths of $m_\text{AB}\sim30.3$ mag, highlighting the intrinsically faint nature of the population. Gas-phase metallicities are inferred by fitting optical emission lines with a grid of BPASS+cloudy photoionization models, while stellar masses are derived from NIRCam photometry through SED fitting. The final sample with secure stellar masses and gas-phase metallicities encompasses only 16 LAEs, occupying regions of standard emission-line diagnostic diagrams consistent with low-metallicity star-forming systems. Although the strong-line metallicity diagnostic R3 appears to decrease with increasing EW, we find no compelling evidence for a strong monotonic relation between EW and gas-phase metallicity when metallicities are inferred through full emission-line fitting. However, galaxies with stronger Ly$α$ emission tend to lie below the average mass-metallicity relation at fixed stellar masses, suggesting that they are preferentially less chemically evolved than typical galaxies of the same mass. We conclude that high-EW LAEs provide useful, though imperfect, analogs of the galaxies thought to drive cosmic reionization, and combining EW with stellar mass may provide a more effective route for identifying the most chemically primitive galaxies.

title: A ${}^{13}$CO Detection in a Massive Molecular Gas Flow in Abell 1795's Central Galaxy
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We present new ALMA ${}^{13}$CO(2-1) observations of the central galaxy in the cool-core cluster Abell 1795, targeting the origin of extended molecular filaments. The filaments extend for 5--7 kpc and are closely drawn up around large radio bubbles inflated by jets from the central active galactic nucleus (AGN). Smooth velocity gradients along their lengths are consistent with entrained flows lifted by the expanding bubbles. Here we detect the northern molecular filament in the low-opacity molecular tracer ${}^{13}$CO(2-1), which can provide a more reliable measure of the molecular gas mass and conditions than ${}^{12}$CO. The velocity structure in ${}^{13}$CO(2-1) is consistent with that of the ${}^{12}$CO(2-1) emission. Using a range of plausible excitation temperatures and covering fractions, we thereby determine a filament molecular gas mass of (0.1--2) $\times \ 10^9 \ \text{M}_\odot$, or down to an order of magnitude below previous estimates. This implies a CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor of $α_\text{CO} =$ 0.4--5 $\ \text{M}_\odot $ (K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2)^{-1}$ in the filament, or $\sim$ 0.1--1 times the standard assumption of the Milky Way value. Direct entrainment by the N radio bubble is now plausible, as it can provide sufficient mechanical energy and buoyant support for the molecular gas flow. Similarly, measured X-ray cooling rates are also now consistent with in-situ condensation of uplifted, low-entropy hot gas. Both formation mechanisms require multiple generations of bubbles at higher filament masses.

title: A clump population framework for star formation across galactic scales
comment: accepted for publication in Nature Astronomy
summary: Whether star formation across different spatial scales and galactic environments follows universal laws remains poorly understood. We investigate cloud-scale star formation in 30 dwarf and disk galaxies. Molecular clouds are identified using a dendrogram algorithm, and their molecular gas masses ($M_{\rm H_2}$) and star formation rates (SFRs) are derived from integrated CO and mid-infrared emission, respectively. We find a consistent $M_{\rm H_2}$--SFR relation across all galaxies, with little sensitivity to galactic environment. Extending the analysis to Milky Way cloud substructures down to sub-parsec scales and 311 diverse nearby galaxies, we find that this relation persists across ten orders of magnitude in molecular gas mass and SFR. A theoretical model in which star formation occurs within dense clumps embedded in molecular clouds reproduces this observed relation. The weak environmental dependence of star formation at the clump scale provides a possible explanation for the nearly universal $M_{\rm H_2}$--SFR relation across galaxies. This framework establishes an observationally grounded connection between star formation in the Milky Way and external galaxies.

title: Thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich Effect in the circumgalactic medium - III: does richness matter?
comment: 19 pages, 8 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We measure the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich Effect in the circumgalactic/intragroup medium (CGM/IGrM) of 7 million $\rm M_{200c} = 10^{12-14}$M$_\odot$ $z \leqslant 1$ DESI Legacy Survey galaxies/groups using ACT+Planck observations, and investigate for the first time how the thermal pressure depends on richness. We detect the one-halo term down to 10$^{12.2}$M$_\odot$ at $5.8σ$. While several mass-richness bins are well described by the standard GNFW thermal-pressure profile ($β=5.49,r_o=0$), others favor a flatter and/or miscentered profile ($β=1.3-4.0,r_o>0.1 \rm R_{200c}$), with the mass dependence of this pattern varying with richness. The wide variety of thermal pressure profiles across mass and richness indicates a range of physical regimes, from dominant thermal feedback to efficient cooling with subdominant thermal feedback, and even substantial cooling. In some mass bins, the super-virial ($\approx2-7 \rm T_{200c}$) temperature floor (the lowest temperature allowed by the data for baryon-sufficient halos) points to significant heating. However, dominant kinetic-mode feedback is not essential anywhere, challenging a universal (ejective)feedback-vs-gravity picture. The slope of the thermal energy-mass relation in IGrM is consistent with self-similarity, but in the CGM it falls below self-similarity by $7.3σ$. This makes halos of relatively low mass and richness the dominant contributors to the universe's thermal energy budget at $z\leqslant1$. We therefore argue that calibrations of thermal energy scaling relations must move beyond the convention of using mass as the sole demarcator and instead incorporate additional intrinsic and environmental properties of galaxies.

title: Mixed modified-gravity--modified-inertia MOND theories
comment: 14 pages
summary: It is plausible that in a more fundamental theory of MOND both gravity and inertia will differ from their Newtonian versions. Such theories, if they embody the basic tenets of MOND, will share its primary predictions with existing theories, which modify either gravity or inertia. But they are expected to differ in their structure and in their secondary predictions. Here, I discuss families of nonrelativistic MOND theories that modify both the kinetic and the gravitational actions of Newtonian dynamics. Each family is spanned by one parameter $0\leη\le 1$, which is the scaling dimension of the deep-MOND limit of all terms in the action. Pure modified gravity ($η=0$) and pure modified inertia ($η=1$) are the end cases in each family. I speak of families, since the modified action terms themselves are not strictly specified, but are treated in rather general terms. These theories are artificial in that they are not based on a single unifying idea that dictates the modification of the two components. But they are still useful in pinpointing some idiosyncracies of such theories. For example, neither of the two modified terms, by itself, leads to MOND phenomenology; only their combined effect does. I show how the two combine to make some of the primary MOND predictions, such as asymptotic flatness of rotation curves, the mass-asymptotic-speed relation, and the deep-MOND, virial, mass-velocity-dispersion ($M-σ$) relation. Another idiosyncracy of such theories is the emergence of different interpolating functions in the kinetic equations of motion and in the gravitational field equations, each relevant under different circumstances, and neither of which have the standard deep-MOND limit. Such examples alert us to the wide range of theories that can lead to MOND phenomenology.

title: From Scaling Relations to Physical Laws: Constraining the Physics of Star Formation Across Local Galaxies
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series
summary: The conversion of cold dense gas, traced by molecular line emission, into stars remains one of the fundamental unsolved problems in galaxy evolution. Observations over the past decades have established empirical relations between gas and star formation, yet their physical origin remains uncertain. Gravity, turbulence, and stellar feedback as main drivers provide fundamentally different pictures of how star formation is regulated, while reproducing remarkably similar galaxy-scale scaling relations. To disentangle the individual importance of each process, not only its mass and distribution, but also its temperature, density, excitation, and chemistry must be probed. However, current or planned (sub)millimetre facilities cannot combine statistical breadth, cloud-scale resolution, and multi-line diagnostics across large galaxy samples. A new, flagship interferometer with increased line sensitivity and bandwidth enables obtaining multi-transition, multi-isotopologue observations of molecular gas at GMC-resolved scales across nearby galaxies, enabling millions of independent measurements of its physical state across a wide range of extragalactic environments. This will transform molecular gas from an empirical tracer into a quantitative probe of the physical processes governing the relation between the dense gas and star formation. With the 2040s landscape of optical and radio facilities, ALMA2040 will facilitate a predictive theory of the conversion of gas into stars.

title: Disentangling Multi-epoch Single-lined Binary Star Spectra to Reveal Interstellar Medium Features via MCMC
comment: 21 pages, 12 figures, 3 tables, accepted for publication in Reasearh in Astronomy and Astrophsics
summary: Diffuse Interstellar Bands (DIBs) are interstellar absorption features with unidentified carriers in the optical and near-infrared spectra. When observed in cool star spectra, they are heavily contaminated by stellar lines. Traditional methods rely on template matching to remove the stellar component, but their accuracy is fundamentally limited by template quality. We present a template-independent algorithm that separates stellar and interstellar features in binary star spectra by exploiting orbital motion: stellar lines shift with changing radial velocity (RV), whereas DIBs remain stationary in the rest frame. The MCMC-RVSD algorithm, implemented as an RV-based Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo framework, fits both components simultaneously. We validated our approach by applying it to mock spectra simulating LAMOST medium-resolution observations. The method precisely recovers the parameters of DIB $λ$6614. It performs reliably for spectra with $R=3000$-$7500$. We applied the method to 434 real binary sources from the LAMOST medium-resolution survey and introduced the MCMC autocorrelation time ($τ_{\mathrm{DIB}}$) to assess the fit quality. Our analysis shows that an RV span $>20$ km s$^{-1}$ is the primary driver of successful line separation. Denser orbital sampling provides further improvement, and the algorithm remains robust against typical observational noise at SNR $>50$ and RV errors $<5$ km s$^{-1}$. Under ideal conditions, our approach yields significantly smaller parameter uncertainties than traditional template matching. Additionally, the MCMC-RVSD algorithm can also handle multi-stellar line contamination, non-Gaussian DIBs and other DIBs by adjusting model and prior settings. This algorithm provides a reliable, general-purpose tool for precise measurement of interstellar features in time-domain spectroscopic surveys.

title: The Radius-Luminosity Relationship for Active Galactic Nuclei with Hierarchical Bayesian Reverberation Mapping
comment: 18 Figures, 33 Pages
summary: Reverberation mapping of active galactic nuclei uses the time taken for variability to travel through the system as a measure of system size, with this size being used to inform estimates of the mass of the central black hole, a technique that has graduated to an industrial-scale effort in recent decades. Such large target-count, multi-year surveys have been consistently undercut by poor light curve quality and the aliasing problems of seasonal observations. These impacts compound with statistical approaches that are not consistent between works and sometimes combine inconsistent statistical frameworks. Here, we present a new end-to-end Bayesian framework for fitting lags at scale in large surveys, simultaneous with the fitting of population models such as the radius-luminosity relation, and formulated in a numerically tractable way. This procedure is a statistically and numerically robust generalisation of the stacking and quality cut procedures of past works, fully marginalising over data uncertainty and data quality. Our approach remains numerically stable when scaling to larger surveys, and can act as a basis for any Bayesian population modelling of large sets of AGN time series observations. Applied to the OzDES sample, we demonstrate that this new approach yields more than double the constraining power on population-level properties like the R-L relationship, and an order-of-magnitude increase in the number of recovered lags and masses. With this method, we go from 24 high quality lag recoveries with traditional methods to a new effective sample size of ~297, all while being robust against random chance false positive measurements.

title: A Comprehensive AGN Inventory for the Dwarf-Dominated RESOLVE and ECO Surveys: Mass-Dependent AGN Types and Occupation Fractions
summary: We catalog Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) in the volume- and mass-limited RESOLVE and ECO surveys using (i) the BPT plot with standard and alternate demarcations, (ii) the BPT plot and VO plots (using [O~I] or [S~II]) to find ``SF-AGN'' with mixed star-forming and AGN classifications, and (iii) mid-IR WISE color selection. Dividing RESOLVE+ECO into dwarf, transitional, and giant galaxies by baryonic mass, we find AGN occupation fractions of 2--5\%, 16--27\%, and 20--48\%, respectively, indicating a steep $\sim$5$\times$ increase across baryonic mass $\sim$10$^{9.7}$ M$_\odot$. These percentages are computed relative to all galaxies in each mass division, including those not searchable for AGN, with numerical ranges representing large systematics between crossmatched emission-line measurements from different SDSS catalogs. Stellar-mass divisions yield similar results. Adding (incomplete) archival X-ray/broadline AGN detections, the dwarf AGN occupation fraction reaches 3--6\%. WISE AGN are detected in $<$1\% of galaxies at all masses with optimized WISE photometry. We show that standard WISE catalog photometry yields high rates of both false positives and false negatives. AGN demographics shift with mass due to correlations with gas content, star formation, and group environment, forming a continuum: SF-AGN at the high-SF end, then ``Bonus AGN'' (defined by alternate literature BPT demarcations), then Composites, then Conventional AGN at the low-SF end. Typical (metal-poor, star-forming) dwarfs most often host SF-AGN, whereas typical transitional galaxies most often host Bonus AGN and Composites. We release homogenized SDSS line measurements, reprocessed WISE data, and UV+mid-IR star formation rates for RESOLVE and ECO.

title: The Mission Market: Flying NASA's Vetted, Unflown Science
comment: White paper submitted to The Space Ideation Challenge 2026
summary: Every year NASA validates more excellent science missions than it can afford to fly. Some of the most promising missions in astrophysics, heliophysics, and planetary science are judged selectable, yet remain grounded indefinitely. Mission Market is an advance market commitment that can fly lower cost missions without competing for federal appropriations. Funding comes primarily from the enormous capital now flowing into artificial intelligence (AI) companies that value generating frontier data for scientific foundation models and is also supplemented by traditional means such as philanthropy and patron-scientists.

title: Stellar Mass Census of $S^4G$ Local Bars
comment: 20 pages, 11 figures, Submitted to ApJ
summary: Bars are stellar structures commonly found in disk galaxies and important agents of secular evolution. Quantifying the stellar mass content of bars provides a physically motivated approach to assess how bar growth depends on galaxy mass and internal structure. We perform a GALFITM multi-band mid-infrared two-dimensional decomposition of 344 barred galaxies from the Spitzer Survey of Stellar Structure in Galaxies ($S^4G$) in the 3.6 and 4.5 $μ$m bands. We estimate the stellar mass associated with each structural component (i.e., disk, bulge, bar, and nuclear point source) and investigate how bar properties correlate with global galaxy characteristics. Our final models consist of 2-4 components per galaxy, with the simplest configuration (disk + bar) typically associated with low-mass systems. We find that more massive galaxies with prominent bulges host more massive bars and higher median bar-to-total stellar mass ratios. These bulges generally present Sérsic indices below 2, consistent with a photometric signature of nuclear stellar disks. Additionally, when we consider the relative bar lengths at a fixed galaxy mass, we find a bimodal distribution where galaxies with bulges host relatively longer bars compared to their bulgeless counterparts. These findings could be the result of different evolutionary paths, possibly linked to different disk formation epochs, allowing bars more time to grow in size and mass. Our study indicates that bar evolution may follow distinct pathways across different galaxy mass regimes, and is likely influenced by secular processes and environmental effects.

title: Dark Matter in the Galaxy: Insights from the Dynamics of Stellar Streams
comment: 27 pages, 5 figures
summary: Dark matter constitutes most of the matter in the Universe, yet its fundamental nature and distribution remain poorly understood. Stellar streams, formed through the tidal disruption of globular clusters and dwarf galaxies, provide powerful tracers of the Milky Way's gravitational potential and dark matter halo. In this review, we examine how stellar stream morphology and kinematics can constrain the halo's structure, shape, and substructure. We discuss key observational signatures, including stream gaps, spurs, and perturbations, and investigate five prominent streams: Sagittarius, GD-1, Palomar 5, Orphan-Chenab, and Cetus Polar. We summarize analytical, statistical, and Bayesian methods used to model stellar streams and infer dark matter properties, highlighting challenges arising from parameter degeneracies, incomplete observations, progenitor uncertainties, and time-dependent perturbations, particularly those associated with the Large Magellanic Cloud. Finally, we discuss how upcoming astrometric and photometric surveys, together with improved dynamical modelling, may strengthen constraints on the Milky Way's dark matter distribution and help distinguish between cold, warm, and self-interacting dark matter scenarios.

title: A Parsec-scale Circumstellar Shell Around VX Sgr: Mass Loss and RSG/TŻO Nature
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: A thin, arc-shaped shell is discovered surrounding VX Sagittarii (VX Sgr), the largest known CSM shell around an RSG at a scale $r\sim0.59\,\mathrm{pc}$. The nebula has an extinction-corrected H$α$ intensity $I_{\mathrm{H}α}\sim38\,\mathrm{R}$ and an ionized mass $\sim0.1\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. The slow $12\,\mathrm{km\,s}^{-1}$ peculiar velocity of VX Sgr and the lack of far-infrared emission in the arc indicate that it is not produced by a bow shock, but is likely instead steady RSG wind or ejecta that is photoionized by a nearby $\mathrm{O}$- or $\mathrm{B}$- type star. The nature of VX Sgr is debated in the literature as a red supergiant/hypergiant (RSG/RHG), super-AGB star, or Thorne--Żytkow Object (TŻO). Using the kinematic age of the Sgr OB1 association, the super-AGB model is disfavored. A spectroscopic test of the arc is proposed to potentially distinguish an RSG from a possible TŻO. The mass-loss rate is estimated from the geometry and emission measure of the shell, finding $\dot{M}\approx4\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. The future interaction of the supernova (SN) ejecta of VX Sgr and the surrounding circumstellar material (CSM) is briefly explored through the mass ratio $Λ$ of the shell and SN ejecta; the interaction would likely not have a significant effect on the SN forward shock.

title: A Search for Dust in the Outflow of the HH212 Class 0 Protostellar System
comment: 25 pages, 9 figures. Accepted for publication in AJ
summary: Perhaps the most visually striking phenomenon during star formation is the ejection of material along the direction of the protostar's rotational axis. Observed in the form of molecular outflows and/or atomic jets, these features carry away mass, energy and angular momentum from the system. Given the known dust content of protoplanetary disks, and the energetics of outflows, it has been suggested that it should be possible to lift dust from disks via winds, yet limited observational evidence has been presented in the literature. Any detection of dust within protostellar outflows not only puts constraints on the dust content in outflows, but if a sufficient amount of dust can be removed from the system, the mass budget for planet formation could also be affected. We present re-imaging of archival, multi-frequency dust continuum observations taken with the Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) towards the HH212 protostellar system. We detect an extension in the dust emission, and using multi-frequency data in Bands 7 and 9, we estimate the spectral index of the emitting dust and the dust mass in the wind launching region. We find a small but still significant amount of dust mass coincident with the molecular outflow cavity. This finding is assessed in relation to the hypothesis that the outflow could be capable of transporting dust away from the HH212 protoplanetary disk.

title: Intermediate- and high-resolution optical spectroscopy on the nascent planetary nebula Vy 2-2: Evidence of binary-star evolution
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. 14 pages, 5 figures, 8 tables
summary: Planetary nebulae (PNe) tend to show spectacular non-spherical shapes whose origin is not fully understood. Crucial information about PNe formation can be obtained by studying their very first stages. We present and analyze new intermediate- and échelle high-resolution spectra of the nascent PN Vy 2-2 to obtain its chemical abundances and a new value for its controversial Abundance Discrepancy Factor (ADF), investigate the internal kinematics and ionization of the nebula, and infer its possible formation processes. Our intermediate resolution spectra reveal many previously unreported nebular recombination (e.g., N$^+$) and forbidden (e.g., [F IV]) emission lines as well as stellar emission lines. Some of the newly detected nebular lines are important to determine the ADF. The derived abundances are subsolar and agree with previous values, while the new value of the ADF(O$^{2+}$)=13.6$\pm$2.6 indicates that Vy 2-2 belongs to the group of PNe with unusually high ADF. Our morphokinematical and ionization structure analysis reveals that Vy 2-2 consists of a relatively high-excitation central region and two low-excitation bipolar lobes. Our data does not show significant shock excitation in the main ionized shell of this PN. A distance of ~1.68 kpc to Vy 2-2 is obtained from the published angular expansion of the central region and its expansion velocity in H$^+$. The inferred kinematical age of ~210 yr supports that Vy 2-2 is a nascent PN. The stellar emission lines suggest a wels-like spectrum although more likely associated with an irradiated close companion than with the central star. Actually, the unusually high ADF, the observed nebular structures, presence of F, among others, point to Vy 2-2 hosting a post-common-envelope binary system. Chemical abundances and circumstellar mass estimates suggest an initial mass $\lesssim$0.9 $M_{\odot}$ for the star progenitor of Vy 2-2.
